evidence.note: Claim: wait lacks an approval mode; a lane filing a person-only approval ends instead of blocking until answered. Probe: read ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py (item/lease judges only, no approval kwarg), ddflow/services/ask/engine.py (pending->answered, E.status), approvals/consume.py (route says re-run --approval ID, no wait). Ran regression first: TypeError wait() got unexpected keyword 'approval' (FAIL), then 3 passed after implementing. Falsifier: if answer wrote elsewhere, wait could never wake.

ddflow brief --agent fix-waitapproval (ranked lessons/rules incl r-bounded-everything, r-tell-dont-discover, r-approval-chat-channel); read wait.py, approvals consume/request/state/canon, ask engine; rule search approval wait lane.

Added ddflow wait --approval <id> mode (wait.py _judge_approval/_wait_approval), CLI --approval flag (navigate.py), route() steering names ddflow wait --approval (consume.py), README quick-ref, regression test tests/test_wait_approval.py (fails unfixed, 3 pass). Ruff clean; regression + consume tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The new flag only teaches `wait` to block; nothing in this change (manifest is only `wait.py`, `consume.py`, `navigate.py`, and the unit test) inserts that wait into the lane driver or orchestrator. Given a lane that files a person-only approval such as `complete.force`, the lane still exits after the ask, and the controller must re-spawn a spend — `consume.py` only appends advice text, and no drivers-as-data step calls `ddflow wait --approval <id>` or re-runs the gated command when the approval reaches `answered`. Auto-resume therefore does not happen.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous wiring gap still holds. The change set is still only `wait.py`, `consume.py`, `navigate.py`, and this unit test; nothing here calls `ddflow wait --approval` from a lane driver or orchestrator step. Given a lane that files `complete.force` / `claim.force` / `gate.skip`, the new test only exercises `A.wait` in-process and then `C.operator_gate` itself, so the lane still exits after the ask and the controller must re-spawn the spend. The regression the intent asks for (the lane resumes and spends on approval) is not what this test runs.

The agent-facing driver doc is the shipped template's stamped region (ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md), regenerated on adopt, not this item's emission path.
